answer: An admission auction sells scarce gate passes by sealed bid. Each epoch sells only 100 slots, and every bid locks for 3 epochs, with a 2-epoch window to challenge and burn fake bids. The vault of bids is public, so bulk buyers cannot hide, and the cipher seal stops one payment backing two identities. A meadow of honest bidders still sets the price, as fake bidders bid against each other. At a 60-unit clearing price, 1,000 identities cost 60,000 units, and doubled demand doubles it. Losers get a refund minus 2%, so honest bidders risk little and bulk buyers pay market price.
